was: Forest Service campground in Oso Canyon above the Santa Ynez River, off Paradise Road north of Santa Barbara; trailheads for the Santa Cruz Trail and the Aliso National Recreation Trail, and the Camuesa OHV route nearby. Only three sites take a trailer or RV (32 ft). PARTLY OPEN: 10 sites first-come, first-served, the other 14 (mostly equestrian) closed after storm damage (FS, checked 2026-09-24). No drinking water. High river levels can close it in winter. --Claude

was: BLM campground on the Deschutes Wild and Scenic River just off Highway 26 north of Madras, 1.6 miles down Mecca Flat Road; the south end of the 7-mile Trout Creek Trail along the river starts here. 13 sites and a group site, first-come, first-served year-round. Vault toilets, no drinking water, no cell. No length is published, but reviewers have brought a 34-ft Class A and 26-30 ft trailers in. The access road is a narrow single lane with a drop-off and few pullouts - reviewers call it bumpy and nerve-racking with a trailer. Goatheads (puncturevine) in the area. --Claude

was: BLM campground on small Duncan Reservoir in the sagebrush west of Silver Lake's dry lakebed: 5 miles east of Silver Lake on OR-31, then 5 miles south on gravel County Road 4-14 (sometimes rough, with washouts that reviewers drove around). Four single sites along the west shore, three of them pull-throughs at the water, plus a group site below the dam; boat ramp, covered picnic area, vault toilet, no drinking water, no food or gas nearby. First-come, first-served, open year-round; stocked trout, ice fishing in winter. Open range - watch for cattle. No published site length. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground in the Blanchard Springs Recreation Area (Ozark NF) north of Mountain View, beside North Sylamore Creek under yellow pines and rock bluffs, near Blanchard Springs Caverns and trout fishing at Mirror Lake. 17 individual sites, all 25 ft - a 23-ft rig fits with little to spare - first-come, first-served, plus reservable group sites. Flush toilets, drinking water and a dump station; no hookups. The campground closes when the creek is high: call 870-757-2211 to check. --Claude

was: Primitive Forest Service campground at about 9,100 ft in Jeffrey pine off Virginia Lakes Road near Conway Summit, south of Bridgeport: US-395 south 13 miles, right on Virginia Lakes Rd for 2.4 miles, then left on FR 139. The FS says several sites take large trailers or motorhomes. Fire rings, bear boxes, vault toilets; no water, trash service or hookups - pack it out. First-come, first-served, late May to mid-October; fills on summer weekends. A free California campfire permit is required for any fire or stove. --Claude

was: Small Forest Service campground on the Chiwawa River 22 miles from Lake Wenatchee, reached from US-2 via WA-207 and the Chiwawa River Road (FR 62); the last 10 miles are very rough gravel and dirt that the FS says may not suit low-clearance vehicles. A handful of first-come, first-served sites, trailers to 30 ft; vault toilet, no water. CLOSED: the FS lists it closed by a road washout after the 2026 Little Giant Fire, no reopening date (checked 2026-09-24). --Claude

was: BLM campground on the Colorado River off SR-128, 22 miles up the river road from US-191 north of Moab, across from the Fisher Towers turnoff; a river-trip put-in with two boat ramps. 21 first-come, first-served sites (cash or check) plus two reservable group sites; toilets, no water or hookups; 14-night limit. No published length, but reviewers report rigs up to 40 ft and trailers. Minimal cell service. The river has dangerous undercurrents. --Claude

was: BLM campground on a bench above Onion Creek near the Fisher Towers, 1.5 miles up gravel from SR-128 (22 miles up the Colorado River road from US-191 north of Moab), with red-rock and La Sal views. 14 first-come, first-served sites (cash or check) plus two reservable group sites; toilets, no water or hookups; 14-night limit. Reviewers have brought fifth wheels and Class As of 32-40 ft. The Onion Creek 4WD road starts here - flash floods in the monsoon. --Claude

was: BLM campground and boat ramp on the North Platte River east of Alcova: WY-220 east 7.4 miles, then 3.7 miles on County Road 316. Eleven sites with RV parking, tent pads, tables and fire rings, first-come, first-served; vault toilet, no water. A drift-boat launch for the Gray Reef stretch. --Claude

was: Small BLM campground on the North Platte River 12 miles from Alcova: WY-220 east 7.4 miles, then 4.2 miles on County Road 316 (washboard). Four sites with tent pads, tables and fire rings, first-come, first-served; vault toilet, no water. Bank fishing. A reviewer's 23-ft-plus trailer fit, but check the loop before pulling in. --Claude

was: Small Forest Service campground on a river terrace of giant cedar and fir between US-12 and the Lochsa River (Lochsa Ranger District). About 7 first-come, first-served sites; aggregate roads, vault toilets, tables and fire rings; RVs to 24 ft - a 23-ft rig fits with little to spare. Seasonal, roughly May-September. --Claude

was: BLM campground (run with PacifiCorp) on the southeast shore of Oneida Narrows Reservoir on the Bear River, north of Preston via ID-34, ID-36 and Oneida Narrows Road, just past Redpoint. 12 first-come, first-served sites, one RV plus one boat trailer or car per site; vault toilets, boat ramp and dock, horseshoe pits; no water or dumpsters. Overnight campers only, 14-day limit. --Claude

was: Large Forest Service campground on Highway 36 two miles west of Mineral (38 miles east of Red Bluff), close to Lassen Volcanic National Park. 50 sites with grills and tables, potable water, vault toilets; trailers to about 25 ft; open mid-May to September. CLOSED for the 2026 season - the FS says it is unsafe to occupy because of hazardous trees (checked 2026-09-24). --Claude

was: BLM campground at the foot of the Caliente Range on the Carrizo Plain National Monument: from Soda Lake Road, 4.5 miles up Selby Road. 13 first-come, first-served sites with tables, fire pits and horse corrals on a packed-gravel loop; accessible vault toilet, three water spigots that may be dry; no garbage service or electricity. Keep rigs to about 25 ft; the monument's dirt roads turn slick and impassable after rain. Spring wildflowers; unreliable cell. --Claude

April-September. --Claude  Island County's park page (2026-10-11): 15 pay campsites, 3 of them RV sites with water only (no electric or dump); all first come, first served, no reservations; campground closed October 1 - April 30. --Claude

was: Fairgrounds RV lot in Turlock off Hwy 99. Full hookups (30/50 amp), cash, first-come first-served - call the number on the gate. No showers or other amenities. Year-round. --Claude

was: Mono County campground in Lundy Canyon off US-395 north of Lee Vining, along Mill Creek among aspens. 36 sites, most fit rigs to ~35 ft; vault toilets, bear boxes, no drinking water. Cash, first-come first-served. Mid-April to mid-November. --Claude

First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay), open year-round. --Claude

was: CCC-built Malheur NF campground in ponderosa pine just off US-395, 17 miles north of Burns (~5,300 ft) - an easy overnight stop that is busy only in fall hunting season. About 24 tent/trailer sites on tight paved loops; the FS says trailers 20 ft and under, but reviewers find 4-5 larger sites that take 25-36 ft rigs (site 1 is paved and roomy) - most sites are short and sloped. Vault toilets, drinking water in summer only, no trash service, no hookups. First-come, first-served, open year-round (Sno-Park permit in winter). Idlewild Loop Trail on site. --Claude

was: The largest of the small Wallowa-Whitman NF forest camps along the Wild and Scenic Lostine River, 11 miles up the Lostine River Road (FR 8210, paved then washboard gravel) from Lostine. 8 tent/trailer sites above the road-side bench plus 5 tent-only sites down by the river; reviewers have fit 23- and 31-ft travel trailers. Two vault toilets, no drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, season June-October. No cell service. --Claude

Vault toilet, no drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, season June-October. No cell service. --Claude

was: Tiny Wallowa-Whitman NF forest camp on the Wild and Scenic Lostine River, 16 miles up the Lostine River Road (FR 8210) - rough gravel past the Lostine Guard Station. 3 sites with tables and fire rings; a reviewer fit a 23-ft travel trailer in large site 3, which has wooden steps down to the river. was: BLM campground at the New Joe's bouldering area in Joe's Valley west of Orangeville, on the way up to Joe's Valley Reservoir. 13 back-in sites, 25-50 ft, with tables and deep fire rings; pit toilets, no water, no trash service, no hookups. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. World-class bouldering; the San Rafael Swell to the east. --Claude

was: Small BLM campground in Cottonwood Canyon within the Joe's Valley bouldering area west of Orangeville. 10 sites, driveways 15-30 ft (seven at 25-30 ft, so pick one of those). No hookups. Cash, check or scan-and-pay, first-come, first-served. --Claude

First-come, first-served for the 2026 season - pay on arrival by cash or check. Next to Libby Creek Willow; Corner Mountain trails nearby. --Claude
